title: The Key To Successful Leadership Succession
paragraphs: Today I will talk about the fundamentals of a successful leadership transition process. I have had the honor of meeting many leaders in various fields. I sat with the President of Israel, shook hands with the Queen, the Queen Mother and the King of Swaziland, and had the opportunity to sit with Mr. Nelson Mandela, the President of South Africa, advise the President of Namibia, and have dinner with him.

I sat and slept in the home of the President of Zambia, sat with world Christian leaders and ate with them, and had the opportunity to sit with civilian leaders and even work with some of them. I have come to the conclusion that the most lacking aspect of leadership training is the area of leadership transition.

80% of leadership conflicts in developing countries occur during transitional periods, either upon the death of the leader, as a result of a coup, or when leadership changes in an organization or political party. But to all of this is added the experience itself in the church. Nothing is more difficult than a leadership transition, because we keep repeating the same mistakes. Therefore, I would like to talk to you about understanding the principles of leadership transfer.

Let me begin with the biggest challenge facing leadership, and I will present it to you in the form of principles. Firstly, leadership is not granted to one generation. Write down this idea, reflect on it, make it firmly rooted in your hearts, and make it a part of you. True leadership is not granted to one generation. If you think this way, you will begin to change your philosophy.

When I talk about leadership, I am referring to someone being appointed as head of a department in a company, or someone being appointed to a position in the church, whether as a deacon, subdeacon, or assistant pastor or pastor. If someone is appointed as a company manager, CEO, or head of a youth group, remember that leadership is not given to one generation. If you are appointed president of a country, democratically elected by the people, leadership is not granted to one generation.

If you settle on this concept, you will suddenly realize that every leader is temporary. Sometimes the weakest temptation for us as leaders is to believe that the world begins and ends with us. Leadership is always transitional. Any leader who believes he is permanent, there is one factor that will end him, and that is death. No matter how terrifying or brilliant a leader may be, death will eventually bring him to an end.

Therefore, it is important to keep the idea of ​​your mortality present in your mind as a leader. The second principle: Leadership that serves only its own generation is doomed to failure. You should never lead while thinking only of your own generation. Whether you are a teacher in a religious school, a classroom teacher in a public school, or a corporate executive in charge of an entire department or branch, remember that your leadership is there to serve not just your generation.

The third principle: God is the God of generations. One way to remember this is to write it this way. God is not addressing you, but rather your inner self. If you study the Bible carefully, you will find that God always reminds those he addresses that he is not addressing them, but rather future generations. Because he thinks on a generational level. Therefore, true leadership, that which comes from God, always thinks in terms of generations. The fourth principle: Success without a successor is failure.

It doesn't matter how successful you are as a leader, and it doesn't matter how much people talk about your great achievements and good deeds, if there is no successor, you are a failure. The fifth principle: If your message or vision dies with your death, you are a failure. No matter how great your vision, no matter how brilliant your ideas about your company, your business, your mission, your country, or your church, if everything dies with your death, you are a failure.

I will talk to you about the vision, and I hope we will discuss this topic tomorrow in a workshop. I will talk about visions, but let me say one thing about them: a true vision from God will always be greater than your lifespan. Therefore, never try to fulfill your vision in your life, for God is greater than that. It will always give you a vision that will remain after you are gone. This means that part of your responsibility as a visionary is to prepare your successor to continue the work.

If your work dies with your death, then you have failed. There are many people you may admire, but in my view they have failed, because they took with them to the grave everything they were supposed to leave for us. Let's talk a little about servant leadership. In the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 20, in the Comments of the Supreme Leader, Jesus Christ, verse 26, he says: “Whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave.”

He then continues, saying, “Just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom, so you must be his servants.” Servant leadership can be defined as follows, and this is my simplified definition: It is the discovery of one's purpose, talents, and abilities, and one's commitment to harnessing them to serve humanity. In other words, it is about discovering what you are supposed to offer to humanity.

Or in other words, it is the willingness to serve your talent at every opportunity. I repeat, it is the readiness to serve your talent at every opportunity. Now, I would like to emphasize the last part of this statement: every opportunity. Because the last part serves as preparation for the first part. To become an effective leader, you must seize every opportunity to serve. I cannot stress this enough. Do n't wait until you are great to be great, you will never reach greatness.

If the bathroom needs cleaning, this is an opportunity to practice your talent. If they need help caring for the youth in your organization, this is an opportunity to serve. If they need someone to clean the building after each session, volunteer. This is an opportunity to offer help. If they need someone to type on the computer, and you are able to do so, then step forward to provide the service.

If someone needs to park their car when entering a parking lot, perhaps you aspire to become a skilled orator, teacher, shepherd, or CEO someday, but you haven't reached that stage yet. That opportunity hasn't come yet, but the opportunity to park the car is available. So, volunteer to park cars before you help people. Servant leadership is serving others at every opportunity. I will give you a practical example of a true leader.

The Lord Jesus, the greatest leader of all time, sent his disciples to a city with these instructions. He said, " Go to the next town. You will find a woman carrying a jar on her head. Ask her where I will eat the Passover. She will show you a place. Go and prepare the Passover until I come." The disciples set out for the city and found the woman, as he had said, carrying a jar on her head. They asked her about the place. She pointed him out to them. When they arrived, they encountered a problem.

There was no servant at the door to wash their feet. There was a habit, a healthy habit. In those days, they wore sandals. The weather was very dusty, and it still is in Palestine today. When you walk in sandals in those streets, dust accumulates on your feet. And when you go to eat with someone, in those days, they would eat, and still do in the Middle East, on the ground. They would place large carpets on the floor, large cushions, and the table would not exceed 1. 5 to 2 meters in height.

They would lie on their elbows and eat. So, to eat in the time of Jesus Christ, you had to recline. To lie down, 12 people in a room on the floor to eat at a table that was two meters high, it was always two meters high. I'm checking if you're listening. You will certainly find that people's feet will be close to or near your face. It was customary in every house to have a servant at the door carrying a basin, so that guests could wash their feet upon entering in preparation for the meal.

In fact, it was considered impolite to eat at the table without washing one's feet for reasons of hygiene. This was not out of religious conviction. So, when they arrived, they found no servant at the door. The twelve men stood outside, arguing, “Where is the servant? We cannot prepare food for the Lord until we are ready, and there is no one to wash our feet.” They were furious and waited for the servant for hours. Jesus came and saw them outside. He asked them: "What are you doing here?"

They replied, "There is no servant." Jesus did not answer them. Instead, he went to the small cupboard, opened it, took the basin, and crossed the street to the well. He dropped a bucket, filled it with water, crossed the street, and brought it back to the door. He placed him on the servant's chair. Then he sat down, took a towel without saying a word, and said: "First." And he washed their feet. Peter. Everyone called out: "Peter". Peter was upset by this.

Therefore, when it was Peter's turn to be washed, Peter felt very ashamed, as did the others, and decided to say something. He said, "Sir, you don't have to wash my feet." Now, many people have interpreted this in a spiritual way, but it is not a spiritual statement. Jesus said, "Peter, unless I wash your feet, you will not eat with us." This statement made it very profound. It wasn't deep. Your feet smell bad. Dirty and smelly.

If you don't let me wash your feet, you won't come in, but will lie on the floor with us and eat. Peter replied, "Lord, wash my whole body." Jesus said, "You are mistaken; you have already paid the price. The only thing that has dust on it is your feet." So he submitted. They entered the house. At that time, everyone felt ashamed. So nobody spoke. There was complete silence. They started preparing the food, and everyone sat down, then lay down, then sat down and ate, and no one spoke.

That was obvious for an obvious reason. They were extremely ashamed. They did not speak. Then Jesus suddenly decided: "Let me speak." Then he asked, "Do you understand what I did there? " "What did you do at the table?" They did not answer. He said, “You see? Even I, your Lord, washed your feet and ministered to you. Why? Because leadership isn’t defined by position, it’s by opportunity. Some of you are looking for leadership, and it’s right there around you. Clean the bathrooms. Dust the floors. Hand out books.

Arrange the cars. Greet people at the door. Stop trying to be elders if you can’t even greet people at the door first. Opportunity is what servants seek. I did everything that happened in this church. I did it all myself. I opened the building myself. I fixed the chairs myself. I played the piano, led the hymns, and then preached myself. I operated the camera myself. I operated the sound myself. I transcribed the tapes myself. You won’t believe it.

We have a staff of 60 full-time workers and another 120 service assistants, but I did everything they did. I cleaned the floor, everything. Anything I asked them to do, I did. That’s why I…” Here now. You are here. Don't seek power, seek opportunity. Real leaders don't go into the bathroom, see a piece of paper on the floor, and ask, "Where's the maintenance man?" No, the paper becomes their personal responsibility. Servant leadership is using your talent at every opportunity, not just when you are visible.

Third, servant leadership is self-service to the world. This is the simplest definition of servant leadership: self-service to the world. All the examples you have heard this week are absolutely true and can be applied in all of these cases. Tiger Woods became great because he served the world. Michael Jordan became great because he served the world. I mean, these men, all they do is serve themselves. They found their talent and serve it to the world and become great.

Jesus said, "The greatest among you is the one who serves." Then he said, "I am a sacrifice and I offer a sacrifice to the world. That is why I am great. " So, should you be great by serving your talent to the world? The word "slave" is important here. Michael Jordan is a slave. That's why he earns $200 million a year, and you can't imagine that you earn even 10% of that. He is a slave. While you are asleep, he is training. While you are asleep, he is running. While you 're asleep, he's in the gym.

While you are asleep, he is practicing shooting for hours every morning. He is a slave to his talent. That's why they seek it. Have you found something you are a slave to so that you can serve it to the world? Now, let's talk a little about the purpose of driving. You are now a leader. I have been greatly respected. You have some credibility. Let's discover the purpose of leadership. In the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 28, verse 17, Jesus mentions the purpose of leadership. He has risen from the dead.

He went to hell, picked up some keys, and then got up again. It is on the other side of the cross. He has triumphed over death, hell, and the grave. He is mighty in all his glory. He is now ready to face the world. Then he says: “I have been given all authority in heaven and on earth.” " You know, when someone gets that kind of power, you're in trouble. If someone becomes your boss, they'll get revenge on you for everything you did to them. 'I wasn't given all the power, now I'll get my revenge.

Didn't you talk to me last month? You parked in my spot. I'm in charge now. I'm going to hurt you.' That's our concept of power. In other words, according to the prevailing leadership philosophy, power is given to suppress those you lead. Power is given to subdue people, to keep them in their place. Doesn't that sound familiar? But look at the mindset of this great leader. He says, 'Because I have all the power, so you go ahead.'" In other words, the purpose of true authority is to liberate the authority of others.

The purpose of true authority is to liberate the authority of others, not to control it. Let me put it another way. An average leader employs others, but a true leader empowers them. That's a huge difference. So, what I don't want in my company are employees; what I seek is the freedom to employ them. I want to create an environment that enables them to utilize their talents and serve the world. I don't want to control people; I want to liberate them.

That's why Christ says, "I have authority in heaven and on earth and under the earth." So, because I have authority in all these areas, go forth and liberate your authority. True leaders are not afraid of their followers' success. Paul and John understood this. When you read their texts in the Bible, you find their attitudes reflected in their letters. John says, " I am glad to see my children flourish in the word of the Lord and prosper."

John says, " Above all, I wish that you would prosper and be as healthy as your son." In other words, their happiness lay in seeing their followers achieve great success. Most of us feel anxious when we start to... They were under our influence and prospered. So, your insecurity manifests itself in the success of others. I repeat, your insecurity manifests itself in the success of others.

If you feel anxious when those around you succeed, you are not a true leader; you are a manipulator, and your insecurity is showing. Now, let's look at... Now that you are a leader, you are harnessing your talent for the world. Your talent has attracted people, and they are inspired by you. But now you know that you will not be in this position forever. How do you choose your successor? I will explain this very briefly. I will be writing a book on this subject next year.

I am writing it because we need some help in this area. First, I will give you a list of people who should not be chosen as a successor. But this list will surprise you. First, never choose someone who likes to see you. What a surprise! What a surprise! What a surprise! If you want someone to succeed you, and... if you want to take the reins and appoint them and install them and prepare them for the future, then here's the shock: Don't choose someone who likes By seeing you. Oh, the shock! If you saw your face!

It only gets worse. Second, don't choose someone who likes and desires your talent. That's a slim chance of succession. Third, never choose someone who wants what you have. Some people only surround themselves with you to get what you have. They don't like you, and they don't care about you. They want to be associated with you for credibility and to further their own ambitions. They want to advance through association. They want your name and your influence. So, they're with you, but not for you.

They like your talent. In fact, I must admit, talent attracts people. But the people your talent attracts aren't the people you'll leave your future to. You know, if you study the Gospel of John, chapter 2, the last three verses, you'll find something interesting. Christ was at the beginning of his ministry, you know, he was starting his work. And the Bible says that when he performed two miracles, people flocked by the thousands. Then it says in the Gospel of John that they believed in him.

They celebrated him and cheered him. The next passage says: But Jesus did not surrender himself to them. Why? Because he knew what was in every person. In other words, this passage is saying: Look, people don't love you; they love your talent. So, you can't trust them. They come by the thousands because of what you do, not because of who you are. Fourth, and this is difficult: Never choose someone who wants your authority. People come into your life and say, "I want your anointing." Bad request.

The wrong person to choose. You know, there was a man in the New Testament who saw Peter, James, and John exercising authority. He was excited and said, "Wow!" He said, " Look, man, I'll give you anything if you give me this authority. I'll offer you money." And he did. Peter turned around and said, "So be it— you and... to hell with the money. May you be struck blind." And the man was struck blind.

Look, there are people who covet your authority, and they come to you in a nice way, you know, saying, "I like your anointing, brother." Look, they are not the right person to leave the organization to. Because what they want is Your authority. James and John were not qualified to succeed Jesus. Why? Because they wanted power. "I want to sit at your right hand, and my brother at your left." Forget the rest. Jesus says, "Where did you get this spirit?" They wanted to monopolize power.

There are some people out there, Lord. They're not like us. Bring down your fire. Eliminate the competition. Jesus says, "Where did you get this spirit, friends?" The same two men, James and John. There are people out there who try to eliminate others in your organization to make themselves the only candidate. They compete for the position, they plot and they flatter, they try to gain power. They are not the right person to choose to succeed you. And it gets worse.

Never choose someone who wants a leadership position for your success. And you can spot them, you know. They're always people who come trying to be nice to you. There's a difference between genuinely wanting to serve the leader and exploiting him. Some people come and say, "I want to serve you." I want to travel with you. I want to be your assistant. I want to do everything you ask of me. "And their motives are easily discernible. Others come, and their attitude is perfectly legitimate.

They know they simply want to appear respectable. They need nothing. If you wish, you can have them accompany you. It's up to you. The attitude. Remember Elisha's first visit to Elijah? Elisha was after something. Power. The first time, he came to Elijah and said, 'I will follow you.'" I will do whatever you want. Elijah said, "Go to your house." Stay away from me. "That was his first reaction. He rebuked him. Then Elisha left. He returned to his house, and stayed there for a few months. God worked in his heart.

He came back in a good spirit. He burned his plow, sold his farm, and roasted the ox. After a few weeks, he appeared at Elijah's door empty-handed. He said, "Will you accept me?" Anything you want from me." Elijah said, "Now you can come with me." If you stay with me, you will gain power. You will receive the service. You will get company. Because you want to serve me now. “You don’t want what I have; you only want to serve me.” And so Elisha received a double portion— his own and Elijah’s.

And he also gained companionship. Second, never choose someone who thinks they are wiser than you. This is crucial. Many people don’t realize how dangerous this is. If you are going to choose a successor, don’t choose someone who is always correcting you, who always thinks you don’t know what you’re doing, who questions your decisions. You know, Peter almost missed this opportunity once. Jesus said, “Let me save you from your future position.” Peter questioned Jesus’ decision.

Jesus said to him, “You are full of Satan.” Get out of this meeting now. "Get away from me, Satan!" Peter never disobeyed Jesus again. He never argued with him again. He never argued with him again. He was wrong. Okay. Now, I've blown out all your reasons for choosing someone. Here they are. Okay, look at that list. This is exactly what you were planning. You want to choose someone who likes your vision. Pastor, I like what you do. Sir, I like your company. You know, you have a wonderful ministry. Great, I like it.

Yes, I also don't have worldly worries. Yes, man, I want to see the poor and needy. Yes, sir. And then save them. I admire your vision. You're wrong. Because whoever likes your vision will take it from you. This is called a split in the institution. Okay, Pastor. What are you going to do now? I've destroyed all your options. Okay. Now let's move on to choosing your successor. This is going to be a surprise. How do you choose your successor? First, choose someone who likes you, not your vision.

I'm going to ask you this question to be sure. Choose someone who likes you, not your vision. This is the most important thing to look for. There's a big difference between these two elements: the vision and you. Don't choose someone who likes your vision. Try to identify the person or people around you—maybe two or three—who genuinely like you. I'll need three chapters in my book to explain what that means. You can tell when someone likes you. Second, choose someone who likes you, not your talent.

Third, choose someone who likes you more than your power. Notice the focus of these principles. They all center on who? You. It's a completely different model of succession. The person who likes you more than your power, influence, talents, and everything that makes you unique—the person who likes you—is the one qualified to take the reins of your future. I'll explain why shortly. Fourth, identify your successor. Choose someone who is willing to protect and defend you, even at the cost of their life.

I wonder if you're qualified to run your boss's company. I wonder if you're qualified to run your pastor's church. Evaluate yourself. Choose someone who is willing to protect you, even at the cost of their life. Fifth, choose someone who is willing to sacrifice. With his life for you.

Not the talented person, not the educated one, not the famous one, not the eloquent speaker, not the charismatic one, not the influential one, but the one who wants to hand over the company, the ministry, the government to someone who is prepared to sacrifice his life for you. Not for the vision, but for you. I know this is new to all of you. And that's why they keep making mistakes in the church, the world, business, and government. Don't hand over the reins to someone you love, but to someone who loves you.

Sometimes, the person you love doesn't love you back. That's why so many family businesses fail. Because sometimes we assume our children love us. You work for years, you build a company, then you hand it over to your son, and five years later he's bankrupt. Why? Because he didn't love you. He didn't appreciate the effort you put into building that company. He didn't appreciate you. Now, remember this point; it's very important. Choose someone who loves you and will take risks for your benefit.

I'm going to give you some tips to start looking in your department, your company, your ministry, your political party. If you want someone to mentor to succeed you in the future, this list is invaluable. At a price. Choose someone who will take risks for your benefit. Okay, let's take some examples here regarding leadership succession. The biblical criteria for choosing your successor are simple: Choose someone who loves you, not your vision, your work, or your talent. Example: Numbers, chapter 11.

This is a very important chapter to read. I don't have time to read it all, so this is your assignment for tonight. Read Numbers chapter 11 in its entirety. It is very moving. In this chapter, we find the introduction of a young man named Joshua, who is a teenager. Joshua is an interesting character. Miriam is known in the Bible as Moses' sister, and Aaron is known as Moses' brother. Joshua is the only person known in the Bible as Moses' servant. He is never known as God's servant. You missed this.

Look, some people want to serve the Lord through your service. That sounds good. No, no, no. If you are qualified to take on the ministry and work, you should come to me to serve me. Because you might only serve me to exploit me and claim that you are serving God. Joshua is never known as the servant of the Lord until after Moses' death. The only title he ever held was "servant of Moses." Now, let's find out why.

In the Book of Joshua and Numbers 11:28, there's a chapter where Moses is commanded by God to transfer His Spirit—and there's a small letter here—to 70 elders to receive His anointing or vision. So, Moses went and chose some people and began ministering to them and sharing His vision. His Spirit is the anointing; call it what you will. As he did this, the anointing, or the vision, began to flow throughout the camp. Some people weren't present at the meeting. Read the chapter; you'll find that.

They were in their tents. But what happened was that the anointing also spread and began to affect some of those who weren't there. They, too, began to say the same things Moses was saying. In other words, they began to speak the same words. " We're going to the Promised Land," whatever the vision was, they began to say the same thing. Joshua was in the camp at that time. He went to visit the people and saw and heard them speaking, and their voices sounded exactly like Moses's. They were speaking the same words.

Joshua came running back, look at this. Joshua son of Nun, who had been an assistant to Moses for a long time, said to Moses: “My lord, my lord, stop them.” Stop them. He said, "There are people in the camp who are taking your job." "This is what he was saying to Moses. These are the ones who have become your rivals. They are just like you. Moses replied, in a reasonable manner: "Are you jealous of me?" " Please write this down. This is the key to knowing who will take over the company.

The one who is jealous for you. The one who wants to protect you. Miriam didn't want to protect Moses; she wanted his position. Come on, remember? Aaron didn't want to protect Moses; he wanted his position. He and Miriam met and were plotting a coup. Joshua was busy protecting Moses. Do you protect your leader? Do you secretly defend him and say, 'Don't say that to my shepherd?' Don't you dare speak like that. You should never say anything like that about him. What are you doing? I'm rebuking you. Stop it.

Or are you participating? You wo n't be eligible for transfer. Are you jealous of your leader? Joshua's eligibility lies in this statement. He was jealous of Moses, the only man who protected and defended Moses. Moses says, 'My son, I wish that all the Lord's people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his Spirit on them.' What a testament to a confident leader! He isn't afraid of others prospering. He also has the same mindset as Miles Monroe."

He says: "Every human being is a potential leader if he wants to be." And I hope they all discover their leadership potential and become like me.” Wow! What a mindset! If that’s true, here’s another example that will shock you. I call it “Love in the Shadow of Denial.” Let me warn you now, this will shock you. Sit up straight. Your religious understanding will change. You’ve been taught all your life that Peter’s denial of Jesus was a bad thing. That’s not true. Christ foretold the denial. So, it wasn’t bad.

He knew it would happen. In fact, Jesus, this is going to be a shock to you now. He was happy it happened. Jesus hoped Peter would deny him. That’s why he told him beforehand, “Make sure you deny me.” By the way, you’ll know when you’re going to deny me; the rooster will crow. In other words, he said, “Look, you have to deny me.” This is part of the plan. "If you don't deny me, it won't work." Isn't that a shock? Now, don't applaud yet. Let me explain why.

Because the condition for Peter to be the successor was that he deny him. Let me explain why. And the reason most of you are unqualified to succeed your leader is that you are unwilling to deny your leader. Please explain. Okay, explain. Love is shown in denial. Let's read it. John 18:10. Then Simon Peter. Let's start with this. Someone drew a sword and struck the high priest's servant, cutting off his right ear. Jesus commanded Peter, "Put your sword back in its place.

May I not drink the cup that the Father has given me?" (John 18). I'll comment on this in a moment. Simon Peter and another disciple in the same chapter follow Jesus. Let's get back to the context. Jesus is in the Garden of Gethsemane praying. These are the most difficult moments. His life. He is about to do his final thing. Let us all say: Love. Let us say it again: Love. You always choose the one who loves you. Jesus is in the garden praying. He knows it is his last moment. He feels the weight of it.

He says, “Stay awake, everyone, because something is going to happen tonight. Something is going to come down.” He is wrestling with his mission. The soldiers arrive with Judas. The Bible says that when they arrived, his disciples ran away. But only one of them… Now you have to understand this. They are soldiers with daggers, swords, spears, and shields. Eleven disciples stand with him, supposedly his closest friends. The only one among all these soldiers who drew his sword and was about to face them was Peter.

Now, where is John, who said he loved Jesus so much? Where is James, who was so attached to him? Where is Bartholomew? Where is the simple little John? Where are these men? Only one was ready to die. Do you understand? The only one who was ready To confront a full guard. And Christ allowed him to brandish the sword and cut off his ear. Why? Christ is investigating to see who loves me. He could have stopped doing it. But he said, "No, I want to see who will love me more." Who loved me more?

I am the only one who drew the sword at the cost of his life, and that was Peter. No problem. He said, "Put it down." Then he healed the man. And then what did he do? He surrendered to these men. They put him in chains, bound him, and led him away. And now they are taking him to trial in the middle of the night. All the other disciples ran away. The Bible says they ran away. Everyone says they ran away. But there is something strange here in verse 15.

Simon Peter and one other disciple, not one of the twelve, were known to the high priest. Look at this. He went with Jesus to the high priest's courtyard. Everyone is a traitor. This is not a proper place for anyone who knows Jesus. The only one who said, "I don't care," I will stay with my boss. I will stay with my boss. I will stay close to my boss. Right now I can't be with him, but I will be there. I will follow him even if it is dangerous. Did you stay with your leader when the whole country criticized him?

Were you proud of your church membership when they called it a sect? Did you stay with the church when they published articles about him in the newspapers and lied to him? Did you keep saying, "I'm still a member"? Or did you decide to back down because you wanted to be accepted by the majority? Did you take a risk when they lied to him and you said, "I still believe him"? Who do you give that support to? Give it to the person who is willing to risk everything for you.

Peter loved Jesus so much that it is said that the other disciple who was known to the high priest went back and spoke to the girl on duty there, and they brought Peter in. Where? Inside. Make sure of that. Peter went into the trial. I mean, there wasn't any other disciple there, just him, standing there in the corner in the middle of the crowd, saying, "I love my shepherd." I need to offer moral support. I need to be there. I don't want my shepherd to be alone. Do you love your leader like that?

Now, he knows that if he is arrested, he may be killed. I think that when Christ looked He turned around in the courtroom and saw Peter in the corner, and realized: "I have found my successor." He's the only one here. All those who boasted about others are gone. Look, the denial was of love. Peter desperately wanted to stay. You missed that fact. He desperately wanted to stay. He could have run away the first time the girl asked him, "Who are you?" He lied for love.

Now, if you are important enough, write this down. He lied for love. He says, "Look, I am not one of them." Why? I want to stay here. Do you love your leader that much?
